entities.summary: Butades (b. 700 BCE, Sicyon) was a renowned artist, musician, or performer of the Classical era, active in Sicyon. Known in the fields of music and theater, Butades was a prominent figure in the Sicyonian artistic scene. He was particularly celebrated for his skill in the lyre and his compositions in the style of the ancient Greeks. Butades' legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his works were performed and admired by later generations of Greeks. The city of Sicyon, where Butades was born and active, was a major cultural center in ancient Greece, and his contributions to the local artistic scene had a lasting impact on the development of Greek music and theater. Butades' connection to the city of Sicyon is a testament to the enduring power of local artistic traditions. Butades' own life and career are shrouded in mystery, with little information available about his personal life or the circumstances of his death in 600 BCE. However, his artistic legacy continues to be celebrated and studied by scholars and music lovers alike.
